name: Gin and Tonic
description: Gin lengthened with quality tonic—cold, sparkling, and botanical.
history: Born from quinine tonic in British colonial practice and perfected as a highball of proportion and ice. Fever-Tree and similar tonics changed the modern home version for the better.
whyItWorks: Tonic’s bitterness and bubbles stretch gin’s botanicals. Plenty of ice keeps the drink crisp instead of watery-warm.
garnish: Optional cucumber or mint depending on gin
steps: Add gin, then pour tonic down a barspoon or gently to preserve bubbles.
Garnish with lime. For Hendrick’s, cucumber is welcome; for Drumshanbo, a grapefruit peel is excellent.
techniqueNotes: Keep tonic cold. Warm tonic dies quickly.
Adjust tonic volume to taste—4 oz is a starting point, not a law.

recommendedBottles.rationale: Floral and cucumber-friendly—the crowd-pleasing G&T gin.
Gunpowder tea complexity; try with grapefruit.
Bright Italian juniper for a clean classic G&T.
